angle: The Four Clicks: a fixed path through Ads Manager that tells you what a campaign is really chasing.
hook: Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing. Most people open an ad account and go straight to the creative. Wrong screen entirely.
body:
Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing.

Most people open an ad account and go straight to the creative. Wrong screen entirely.

Meta doesn't chase "good leads." It chases whatever number you told it to chase, in a setting most people never open.

Here's where that setting lives. Ads Manager → your campaign → the ad set → the line that says Performance goal.

That one line tells Meta what to go and find more of: cheapest lead, or a lead that matches people who did something specific after they filled the form.

If nobody ever told Meta what happened after the form, it can only optimise for the form itself. That's why cost per lead can look great while nothing after it improves.

Across nine Meta ad accounts we've run, generating 7,341 lead-form submissions, every lead is counted straight from Meta's lead centre. What we haven't always known — and what most advertisers never check — is what happened next in the business. That gap is the whole story.

Before you touch the creative on Monday, open that one screen and read what it's actually set to chase.

If you want someone to walk your account through this for free, that's what an audit is for.

#metaads #digitalmarketing #adsmanager

slides.text: Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing.
Most people judge it by the creative. Wrong screen entirely.
Open Ads Manager. Click into the campaign that's spending the most.
Click into the ad set inside it. This is where the real setting hides.
Look for the line called Performance goal. Most people have never opened it.
It tells Meta what to go and find more of. Not creative. This.
It might say cheapest lead possible. Or it might say something else.
If it says cheapest lead, Meta stops looking the moment someone fills the form.
It never learns what happened after. Nobody sent that back in.
Check this before the creative. It decides who Meta goes and finds.
The creative gets the blame. The setting was never even opened.
